answer: The mechanism is a staked identity bond: each agent locks a fixed deposit of chain value that stays slashable until it survives several honest epochs. Votes and rewards weight by stake, not headcount, and every new identity pays a non-refundable fee plus a proof-of-work hurdle. A Sybil attacker minting ten thousand bots must fund ten thousand deposits at once, and a tundra of fakes earns no more than the capital locked; detection slashes it. Cost: aggregate bond, burned fees, wasted compute, so a tide of throwaway keys stops paying and forging an onyx token of trust makes flooding irrational.
